# An async.query over an answer that is itself an option holds its value as
# an option of one, and Go's is a pointer to the pointer: putting the answer
# in was written as a conversion of *T to **T, which does not compile.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func fetchOne(k int, life async.Lifetime) async.Result[option[int]] {
    return {ok=k}
}

// The handler's `value` is this component's prop, not the query's.
component one[F any](
    n        int,
    :value   option[int] = null,
) F {
    async.query #query(
        on=n,
        fetch=fetchOne,
        @load(got) {
            value = got
        },
    )
}

component main ui.node {
    var got option[int] = null
    one(n=3, :value=got)
    ui.text #shown(value="{got.or(0)}")
}


func testHandlerWritesItsOwnValue(t test.Test, c main) {
    t.wait(func() => c.shown.value == "3", 3000)
}

ui.window {
    main
}
-- testrun/fyne/go/app.sngl/main/1 --

      "Desc": "HandlerWritesItsOwnValue",
      "Passed": true
    }
  ]
}
